selected_policy: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)

criterion_evaluations.criterion: Anterior cervical discectomy must be performed with a cervical fusion due to the iatrogenic instability/increased disc degeneration of the anterior cervical discectomy procedure.
criterion_evaluations.patient_evidence: The submitted records include an MRI report (mri_report.txt) which states 'Cervical kyphosis noted on supine MRI'. While the MRI doesn't explicitly state fusion, the clinical indication is 'Fixed Cervical Kyphotic Deformity', and the surgical plan notes 'Proposed Procedure: CPT 22220 (C5-C6)', implying a level specific to the deformity. The physician note (physician_note.txt) also mentions 'Diagnosis: Fixed Cervical Kyphotic Deformity (C5-C6)' which aligns with the MRI findings and the surgical plan.

criterion_evaluations.criterion: Anterior cervical discectomy is considered medically necessary when performed with a cervical fusion
criterion_evaluations.patient_evidence: The submitted records include an MRI report (mri_report.txt) which states 'Cervical kyphosis noted on supine MRI'. The physician note (physician_note.txt) mentions 'Diagnosis: Fixed Cervical Kyphotic Deformity (C5-C6)' and proposes CPT 22220 (C5-C6). This strongly suggests the procedure is intended to address the kyphosis, which typically requires fusion for stability.
